cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?
